texts: In ischaemic heart disease, complete revascularization leads to reverse remodelling: the left ventricular ejection fraction rises and the end-diastolic volume falls: B is the answer.
The more completely the ischaemic muscle is revascularized, the more of it recovers.
Recovery after valve operations is slower and less predictable than the other statements claim.
